title: Changing the weather

fn.en: Talk about climate and extreme weather; talk about recent events and ongoing changes.

items.why: find names a completed result, so the simple form is used.
since needs a perfect form, not the present continuous.
A finished number of completed pieces takes the simple form.
A change still in progress takes the continuous form.

tts: Welcome to The World Today. Today we’re talking about extreme weather.

Recently there seem to have been a lot of extreme weather events. While there have always been strong winds and tropical storms, many scientists now agree that climate change has been causing higher temperatures, and more storms, floods and droughts.
It is a serious situation, and although governments have been trying to reduce pollution and stop the global temperature rising, we haven’t been very successful so far.
With us in the studio today we have Neil Clough, our science correspondent, who has been researching ways in which scientists around the world have been trying to artificially control the weather.
Well, if these changes in weather patterns have been happening as a result of global warming, then we should try to prevent further warming, by reducing pollution and protecting trees.
However, scientists have been exploring another method. It seems possible that we might be able to do more to control the weather directly.

items.q: What do many scientists now agree about?
o: That climate change has been causing higher temperatures and more storms
That the weather has not changed

items.q: How successful have governments been so far?
o: Not very — they have been trying but have not got far
They have not tried at all

items.q: What has the science correspondent been researching?
o: Ways of controlling the weather artificially

tts: Scientists have been working on techniques to create or prevent rain for quite some time now. The best-known method is called cloud seeding. This involves putting chemicals into the air to encourage water in the air to form clouds, and hopefully rain.
So if we can make it rain when we want, why do we still have droughts?

Unfortunately it isn’t that simple. If there is a drought, there probably won’t be any clouds in the sky at all. The only thing you could do is seed the clouds when there are some, and save the water.
Hurricanes form in warm tropical waters. As the seas get warmer, there are likely to be more of them. But it seems possible that we could use cloud seeding to cool the seas down.
But is it a good idea to put chemicals into the atmosphere?
One group of scientists in Geneva have been experimenting with lasers. Their experiments have shown that pulses of light can be used to make rain clouds, without any chemicals at all.

items.s: Cloud seeding involves putting chemicals into the air.
Cloud seeding solves droughts easily, because there are always clouds.
Warmer seas are likely to produce more hurricanes.
The team in Geneva have been experimenting with lasers.
The laser method still needs chemicals.

tts: In recent years there has been a noticeable increase in extreme weather events.
Many scientists now agree that climate change has caused this increase.
The science correspondent has just finished researching ways in which scientists have been trying to artificially control the weather.
These scientists have been exploring various techniques, including cloud seeding, over the past few years.
Recently one team of scientists in Geneva has discovered a way to use lasers to control the weather.

items.sit: You want to say the effort has gone on a long time and is not finished.
o: I’ve been trying to fix it all morning.
I’ve tried to fix it all morning and I still am.
I try to fix it since the morning.

o: I’ve painted the kitchen, that’s why I’m covered.
I paint the kitchen since two hours.

I’ve been writing three reports this month.

write.q: Write about how the weather, or one thing about your city, has changed over the last ten years. Use the present perfect continuous for the changes still going on, and the present perfect simple for the results that are already finished.
plan: what you have been trying to do yourself
write.model: Over the last ten years the summers here have been getting longer and drier. The first heatwave used to arrive in July; this year it has already arrived twice, and it is only June. The winters have been changing too — there has been less snow every year since about 2018, which sounds pleasant until you talk to anybody who grows anything. The city has done some things. It has planted about four thousand trees along the main roads and it has banned burning in the private sector. What it has not done is anything about the dust. I have been trying to keep the windows shut from May to September, which is not much of a plan, but it is the only one I have.

speak.q: Talk for about a minute about how something near you has changed. Say what has been going on, and what has actually been achieved.
speak.model: The summers here have been getting longer and drier — the first heatwave used to come in July and this year it’s already been twice, in June. The city has planted about four thousand trees, which is something. But nobody’s done anything about the dust. I’ve been keeping the windows shut since May, which isn’t much of a solution.
